newsitem.title: VATICAN: Cuban minister attends Roman Catholic mass.
newsitem.headline: Cuban minister attends Roman Catholic mass.

text.p: A Cuban government minister has attended a Roman Catholic mass in an official role for the first time in a further sign of improving relations between Havana and Rome, Vatican Radio said on Tuesday.
The radio said Culture Minister Armando Hart officially attended a mass in Havana Cathedral on Sunday to celebrate the Catholic feast of the Immaculate Conception.
"It is the first time that a member of the Cuban government has taken part officially in a mass," the radio reported.
"The gesture appears even more significant, ahead of Pope John Paul's planned visit to Cuba in 1997," it said.
The Polish-born Pontiff, an implacable opponent of communism, met veteran Cuban President Fidel Castro at the Vatican on November 19 in a historic encounter.
Castro, one of the world's few remaining communist leaders, invited the Pope to visit Cuba next year.
Both sides said the invitation had no strings attached and had been accepted by the Pontiff, who has visited ever other Spanish-speaking country in Latin America.
Shortly after Castro took control in 1959, Cuba was declared a socialist state. Some 350 Catholic schools were nationalised and more than 100 priests expelled.
Freedom of worship and religious instruction are limited to church premises.
